title: alerts event, version 1
description: One event published by risk-engine to the alerts topic. kind says which of three event kinds it is, and the object named after the kind carries its content: a space weather level derived from one SWPC value, a close approach found by a screening run, or the summary of one screening run. Every level here is derived mechanically by SpaceFlux from public data; none is an official NOAA scale level, a forecast, or a notice to act. Not related to SWPC's swpc.alerts product: an alerts event is a derived result, never an SWPC alert, watch or warning. See docs/data/topics.md and docs/adr/0007-alerts-topic.md.

schema_version.description: Major version of this contract. Always 1 for events written against this file.

kind.description: Which kind of event this is. space_weather_level: a derived G, R or S level, none, no data, or the end of a satellite series, for one series, published on a change, a correction, or a periodic refresh. close_approach: one close approach within the report distance found by one screening run. screening_run: what one screening run covered and what it did not screen.

rules_version.description: Version of the rules the event was derived under, raised by hand whenever a threshold, a rule, or a screening setting changes (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md and docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md), including any change to the station stack list risk-engine/src/main/resources/screening/stacks.json. It is part of every event_id and of run_id, so reprocessing under new rules publishes new events instead of being dropped as duplicates.

event_id.description: Identity that consumers deduplicate on, because delivery is at least once. It is built only from fields of the event, so a producer retry or a reprocessing run under the same rules writes the same identity for the same event. It starts with the kind, a slash, rules_version, and a slash. The construction per kind is in docs/data/topics.md.

produced_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time at which risk-engine produced the event. Always ends in Z. It says when the event was written, not when the data was measured or fetched; see fetched_at and freshness_reference for those.

utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC time ending in Z. The pattern enforces the shape because format is only an annotation by default in draft 2020-12.

runId.description: Identity of a screening run: its window_start as written in the event, a slash, and rules_version, for example 2026-09-29T05:20:09Z/1 (docs/data/topics.md).

catalogNumber.description: NORAD catalog number, as in raw.gp.

role.description: The role an object was screened in. Every watchlist object is also screened as a catalog object.

code.description: A lower case code. The known values are listed in docs/data/topics.md. The set is open: a consumer shows an unknown code with its reason text rather than rejecting the event.

spaceWeatherLevel.description: The state of one series after a change, a correction, or on a periodic refresh: G from planetary Kp (one series, no satellite), R from GOES 0.1-0.8nm X-ray flux, or S from GOES >=10 MeV integral proton flux (one series per satellite for R and S; satellites are never merged). The state is a derived level, none (a valid value below level 1), no data (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 5.3), or ended (Section 5.4). One event describes one sample or one 3 hour interval, never an event with a start and an end.

scale.description: NOAA Space Weather Scale the level is derived on: G (geomagnetic, from Kp), R (radio, from X-ray flux) or S (solar radiation, from proton flux).

product.description: The raw.swpc product the value came from; fixed by scale.

state.description: level: a valid value at or above level 1, with derived_level set. none: a valid value below level 1. no_data: the newest record was rejected, or the newest time_tag of any record of the series with a usable time_tag is older than the series' age limit (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 5.3); never to be read as none. ended: R or S only, the series of this satellite stopped because another satellite's records took over SWPC's primary file (Section 5.4); it reads as no data and is no longer the current series of its scale.

derived_level.description: The derived level, 1 to 5, present only when state is level. Derived by SpaceFlux from one value with the thresholds in docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md; not SWPC's own issued scale level.

derived_label.description: Readable form of the state: the scale letter and level (for example G4), none, or no data (used for both no_data and ended).

previous_state.description: The state this series (for a new sample) or this Kp interval (for a revision) had before the event. Absent when risk-engine held no earlier state, for example after a restart.

previous_derived_level.description: The derived level before the event, present only when previous_state is level.

trigger.description: level_change: the series' current state differs from its previous state (including a change into or out of no data or ended, and the first state known after a start). revision: SWPC sent a different Kp value for an interval already seen; always published, including a revision to none; G only. When the revised interval is the newest one, the revision also sets the current state and is the only event published for it; a revision of an older interval replaces only that interval's state. restatement: SWPC's value is unchanged, but a later record showed that an earlier sample, published as none, lies on the edge of a zero run, so it is restated as no data (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Sections 5.1 and 5.2); R only; it replaces that sample's state and says nothing about the current state. refresh: no change of state; the series' current state repeated with its newest record, so a consumer can tell a quiet current series from a stale one. Published when newer records arrive for the series without changing its state, and by a timer fallback when nothing went out for the series within its interval (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 5.3); level or none only.

derived_from.description: Readable name of the measurement the state is derived from, including the satellite for R and S, for example SWPC estimated planetary Kp, or GOES-16 X-ray flux 0.1-0.8nm.

estimated.description: True for G: SWPC calls planetary Kp estimated, and a value can be revised, so the level for an interval can change or disappear. False for R and S, whose GOES values SWPC does not label estimated.

satellite.description: GOES satellite number the value came from, for example 16. Required for R and S; absent for G, which is not measured by one satellite.

band.description: X-ray passband the R level is read from, as SWPC writes it. R only.

channel.description: Integral proton energy threshold the S level is read from, as SWPC writes it. S only.

value.description: The value the state is derived from, as received. Present when state is level or none, and on a restatement.

unit.description: Unit of value: Kp index (dimensionless, in thirds), W m-2 (X-ray irradiance), or pfu (protons per cm2 s sr).

xray_class.description: Optional, only on R events in state level from GOES-16 or a later satellite: the X-ray class of value, M or X, truncated rather than rounded to one decimal, for example M1.0, X3.9 or X20.0 (the X number continues past 10). Derived as docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 2.4 defines. Its letter and number agree with derived_level (R1 M1.0 to M4.9, R2 M5.0 to M9.9, R3 X1.0 to X9.9, R4 X10.0 to X19.9, R5 X20.0 and above). It describes this one value, not a flare.

time_tag.description: SWPC's own time_tag of the source record, as sent. For Kp it has no zone designator.

interval_start.description: G only: start of the 3 hour UTC interval the Kp value describes, equal to time_tag read as UTC (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 1.3).

interval_end.description: G only: end of the 3 hour UTC interval, 3 hours after interval_start.

sample_time.description: R and S only: the UTC time_tag of the GOES average the value is.

averaging_period_s.description: R and S only: length of the average in seconds, 60 for X-ray flux and 300 for proton flux.

fetched_at.description: fetched_at of the raw.swpc event the value came from: when ingest received it. Replayed or archived data therefore shows its real fetch time and is never shown as current.

source_url.description: source_url of the raw.swpc event the value came from.

freshness_reference.description: The newest time_tag, as UTC, of any record of this series with a usable time_tag that risk-engine held when it produced the event, including rejected values, zeros and edge values (for G, the newest interval_start); docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Sections 5.1 and 5.3. A consumer judges staleness by comparing the current time with it against the age limit in Section 5.3. Absent only when the series never had such a record.

no_data_since.description: no_data and ended only: the time from which the series has no data, as docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Sections 5.2 to 5.4 define it. For a rejected newest record, its time_tag, moved back to the first restated edge sample when a zero run restates earlier samples (so it can point at a well formed record); for the age limit, the time the limit was passed, which is not when data stopped, so a surface shows freshness_reference, the last record's time, next to it; for ended, the series' newest time_tag; for a restatement, the restated sample's time.

no_data_reason.description: no_data only: rejected when the newest record received for the series was rejected (Section 5.1), which is also the reason at the start of a zero run even when no_data_since points back at a well formed edge sample; zero_run_edge when the sample would be none but lies on the edge of a zero run of X-ray records (Sections 5.1 and 5.2), always the reason on a restatement, and on a level_change in practice only after a restart, since otherwise the series is already in no data from the zeros when an edge value after them arrives; age_limit when the newest time_tag of any record of the series with a usable time_tag is older than the series' age limit (Section 5.3).

restated_by_time_tag.description: restatement only: UTC time_tag of the first zero record of the run that showed the restated sample was on its edge.

timer_refresh_at.description: Timer fallback refresh only: the tick of the fallback timer (docs/risk/space-weather-scales.md Section 5.3) that produced it. Absent on a refresh sent on arrival of newer records. Part of the identity, because a timer refresh repeats the newest record an earlier event already carried.

ended_by_satellite.description: ended only: the satellite whose records at or after this series' newest time_tag ended it.

screenedObject.description: One object of a close approach pair, with the element set age at the time of closest approach.

element_age_days.description: Time of closest approach minus the element set epoch, in days. Negative when the epoch is after the time of closest approach. Position uncertainty grows with it (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Section 4).

name.description: OBJECT_NAME of the element set used, when it has one.

closeApproach.description: Two public element sets, propagated with SGP4, that come within the report distance of each other in one screening run's window. Not a collision probability and not an operational conjunction assessment (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Section 5).

run_id.description: The screening run that found the approach; its screening_run event carries the same run_id.

window_start.description: Start of the run's screening window.

window_end.description: End of the run's screening window.

watchlist_object.description: The watchlist object the search was run for.

other_object.description: The catalog object it came close to, which can itself be on the watchlist.

miss_distance_m.description: Distance between the two propagated positions at the time of closest approach, in metres, at the precision computed. Its uncertainty is at least of the order of kilometres (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Sections 4 and 5).

relative_speed_m_per_s.description: Relative speed at the time of closest approach, in metres per second.

screeningRun.description: What one screening run covered, and every object and pair it did not screen, with the reason. The run is stale 24 hours after window_start and always after window_end (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md). No approaches means only that no searched pair's SGP4 propagation came within report_distance_m; objects not in the input, rejected, not screened, or in a suppressed pair are not covered, and the uncertainty of every distance is of the order of kilometres (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Section 5).

window_start.description: Start of the screening window: the fetched_at of the newest raw.gp event among the element sets the run used (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Section 3.2).

window_end.description: End of the screening window, 7 days after window_start.

input_fetched_at.description: fetched_at of the newest raw.gp event among the element sets the run used. A run's results are stale 24 hours after window_start, and always after window_end, under the staleness rule for screening results in docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md. Equal to window_start in this version; kept as its own field because it states where the data came from, not how the window was chosen.

report_distance_m.description: Miss distance at or below which an approach is reported, in metres (docs/risk/orbital-conventions.md Section 3.5).

coverage.description: Counts of what the run covered. Every pair is exactly one of not screenable, suppressed, removed by the prefilter, or searched, so pairs equals pairs_not_screenable plus the length of suppressed plus pairs_removed_by_prefilter plus pairs_searched.

watchlist_accepted.description: Watchlist objects screened in the watchlist role.

catalog_admitted.description: Objects admitted in the catalog role, watchlist objects included.

pairs_not_screenable.description: Pairs with an object that has no usable track in the window.

pairs_removed_by_prefilter.description: Pairs whose radial bands never come within the report distance.

approach_count.description: Number of close_approach events the run published; equals the length of approach_event_ids.

approach_event_ids.description: event_id of every close_approach event of this run, so a consumer can tell when it holds all of them.

suppressed.description: Pairs not screened for close approaches, with the separation sampled over their joint screenable span. The true minimum between samples can be smaller than min_separation_m.

mechanism.description: Why the pair was not screened; known values in docs/data/topics.md.

detail.description: Readable explanation, as risk-engine wrote it.

min_separation_at.description: UTC time of the smallest sampled separation.

stack_entry_may_be_stale.description: True when a pair listed in the same station stack separated beyond the co-orbiting bound.

rejected.description: Objects rejected before any pair was formed, once per role they were rejected in.

reason.description: Readable reason, as risk-engine wrote it.

not_screened.description: Admitted objects whose track does not cover the whole window.

screened_until.description: Last good time, present only for kind stopped_in_window.

reason.description: Readable reason, as risk-engine wrote it.

epoch_after_start.description: Objects screened by propagating backward from an element set whose epoch is after the window start.

seconds_after_start.description: Epoch minus window start, in seconds.

differing_copies.description: Differing entries for one catalog number in the inputs; the entry with the newest epoch was used and each other entry is listed.

used_name.description: OBJECT_NAME of the entry used, when it has one.

used_epoch.description: Epoch of the element set used.

dropped_name.description: OBJECT_NAME of the entry not used, when it has one.

dropped_epoch.description: Epoch of the element set not used.

dropped_from.description: The input list the entry not used came from.

elements_differ.description: False when only the name differs.
